cards.claim: With constant acceleration the average acceleration over any interval equals that constant, which gives v = v0 + a t.
cards.quote: Suppose that an object is moving in x-y plane and its acceleration a is constant. Over an interval of time, the average acceleration will equal this constant value.

locator.section: 3.8 Motion in a plane with constant acceleration

cards.claim: For constant acceleration the displacement equals the average velocity (v0 + v)/2 times the time interval, giving r = r0 + v0 t + (1/2) a t^2.
cards.quote: Then, over this time interval t, the average velocity is (vo + v)/2. The displacement is the average velocity multiplied by the time interval :
cards.equation: \vec r=\vec r_0+\vec v_0 t+\tfrac12\vec a t^2

locator.section: 3.8 Motion in a plane with constant acceleration

cards.claim: Motion in a plane with constant acceleration can be treated as two independent simultaneous one-dimensional constant-acceleration motions along perpendicular directions.
cards.quote: That is, motion in a plane (two-dimensions) can be treated as two separate simultaneous one-dimensional motions with constant acceleration along two perpendicular directions.

locator.section: 3.8 Motion in a plane with constant acceleration

cards.claim: The constant-acceleration kinematic equations do not apply to uniform circular motion: there the acceleration has constant magnitude but changing direction.
cards.quote: The kinematic equations for uniform acceleration do not apply to the case of uniform circular motion since in this case the magnitude of acceleration is constant but its direction is changing.

cards.claim: The vector equations v = v0 + at and r = r0 + v0 t + at^2/2 do not depend on a choice of axes; they may be resolved along any two independent axes.
cards.quote: The vector equations (3.33a) and (3.34a) do not involve any choice of axes. Of course, you can always resolve them along any two independent axes.

The shape of a trajectory is not fixed by the acceleration alone; it also depends on the initial position and velocity (under gravity it may be a straight line or a parabola).
cards.quote: The shape of the trajectory of the motion of an object is not determined by the acceleration alone but also depends on the initial conditions of motion ( initial position and initial velocity). For example, the trajectory of an object moving under the same acceleration due to gravity can be a straight line or a parabola depending on the initial conditions.
